title: Relationship Banking Basis Note: The Relationship Balance Behind the Personal Checking Rules
content:
Every Personal Checking rule that speaks of a relationship balance uses one basis, taken at close of business on the measurement date.

**Clauses in force.**

1. A checking account with a negative ledger balance contributes zero to the sum rather than reducing it.
2. Outstanding mortgage principal is added only for tiers whose setting says that mortgage principal counts toward the relationship balance, and only for loans in active, delinquent or forbearance status.
3. For the monthly maintenance charge waiver the measurement date is the statement cycle closing date. For the Private Client Checking entry test and for a tier conversion it is the frozen date on which the request is handled.
4. Deposits that are pending and have not posted do not count.

**Clauses no longer in force.** Two clauses of this basis have been superseded by the current charter and are recorded here only so that no reader applies them:

- the clause composing the figure as the customer's deposit balances at the bank summed across checking, savings and certificate holdings in the customer's own name is **no longer in force**;
- the clause stating that credit card balances, auto loan balances and safe deposit box rentals never count is **no longer in force**.

Neither withdrawn clause may be used to work out a relationship balance, and neither is restated here as a rule.

**Points of judgement on the clauses that stand.** The measurement date differs by the question being asked, so one customer can have two correct relationship balances on the same day: one struck at a cycle closing date for a waiver, another struck on the day a conversion or an entry test is handled. A checking account 40.00 below zero contributes 0.00 and not minus 40.00. A mortgage in a status other than active, delinquent or forbearance contributes nothing even on a tier whose setting counts mortgage principal.

superseded_clauses: the customer's deposit balances at PCB summed across checking, savings and certificate holdings in the customer's own name
Credit card balances, auto loan balances and safe deposit box rentals never count.
